sentences.text: Today's topic is very important.
How to Speak English at a Police Station.
Sometimes, we need to go to a police station to report a lost item, ask for help, or give information.
It can feel stressful, but knowing some basic English phrases can help you feel more confident.
Asking for help at a police station.
If you need help, you can go to a police station and talk to an officer.
Common phrases, excuse me, I need help.
Can I speak to a police officer?
I don't speak English well.
Can you speak slowly?
Can you help me please?
It's an emergency.
Where is the nearest police station?
Excuse me, I need help.
Of course, how can I help you?
I lost my wallet.
Okay, can you tell me where you lost it?
And tip, if you don't speak English well, you can say, can you write it down please?
Reporting a lost item.
If you lose something, you can report it to the police.
Common phrases, I lost my wallet.
I lost my phone.
I can't find my passport.
Where can I report a lost item?
I lost my bag in the park.
Can you help me find it?
Example conversation.
Hello, I lost my passport.
When did you lose it?
This morning at the bus station.
Can you describe it?
Yes, it's a red passport with my name inside.
Tip, keep a copy of important documents, like your passport on your phone.
Reporting a crime or accident.
If you see a crime or are in an accident, you might need to talk to the police.
Common phrases, I need to report a crime.
Someone stole my bag.
There was a car accident.
I saw someone stealing a phone.
Can you call an ambulance?
I need to make a police report.
Example conversation.
Hello, I need to report a crime.
What happened?
Someone stole my phone.
Where did this happen?
At the shopping mall 30 minutes ago.
Tip, try to stay calm and give clear information.
Polite language and body language when talking to police.
How to be polite in English.
Use please and thank you.
Speak calmly and clearly.
If you don't understand, say, can you repeat that please?
Good body language when talking to police.
Stand still and relaxed.
Make eye contact, but don't stare.
Keep your hands visible.
Don't put them in your pockets.
Tip, in some cultures, people talk loudly or use a lot of hand movements.
In English speaking countries, staying calm and respectful is very important when talking to the police.
How police stations work in different countries.
Police stations are different in every country.
Some important things to know.
In the UK, police are usually friendly and can help with directions.
In the USA, if you call 911, police will come to help in an emergency.
In some European countries, police officers may speak English.
In some countries, you need a translator to communicate with the police.
Tip, before traveling, check emergency numbers in the country you're visiting.
How to contact police in a foreign country.
If you are in a foreign country and need help, find the nearest police station, search on Google Maps.
Ask for a translator if you don't speak the language.
If your passport is lost, go to your embassy.
If you don't feel safe, call the emergency number like 911 or 112.
Common phrases, I don't speak Spanish, French, etc.
Can you help me in English?
Can I call my embassy?
Do you have a translator?
Tip, always save your embassy's phone number on your phone when traveling.
Staying safe in final tips.
Stay calm and polite.
Give clear information.
Ask for a translator if needed.
Always carry an ID or a copy of your passport.
If you feel unsafe, ask for help.
Now you know how to speak English at a police station.
I hope this episode helps you feel more confident if you ever need to talk to the police.
Thank you for listening.
